title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: No computational error: the matrices, the identities for id−ρ and id−σ, and the determinants 3 and 0 are all correct.

Minor imprecision: 'ne sont pas tous deux des automorphismes' understates the situation. id−σ is never an automorphism (rank 1 in all characteristics). id−ρ is an automorphism over Z[1/3] but not over Z.

ideas.what: Rewriting the local 'coboundary' conditions ξ = α0−ρ(α0) and η0 = β0−σ(β0) as membership in images of 1−ρ and 1−σ, then computing these explicitly via matrices.
ideas.modern_name: Coboundaries / Tate cohomology of cyclic groups acting on Z²: H¹(Z/3, M) = Z/3 and H¹(Z/2, M) = 0 for the elliptic stabilisers of SL2(Z)/GL2(Z).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (cohomology of cyclic groups; Serre, Brown, etc.)

ideas.what: Replacing the non-smooth parameter scheme Σ_{ρ,σ} (in ξ, η) by a finer cover Σ̃ parametrised by the 'primitives' α0, β0, which is apparently smooth. This is motivated by the degeneration of id−ρ in characteristic 3 and the rank-1 nature of id−σ.
ideas.modern_name: Smooth (torsor-like) cover / resolution of a parameter scheme by adding 'primitive' variables, analogous to passing from a Lang-type image to its source.
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to the unpublished Longue Marche (1981) material; not in the published texts as far as known.

missed.claim: A scheme-theoretic (over Z) treatment of the loop equations for the elliptic generators ρ (order 3) and σ (order 2), with explicit analysis of bad behaviour at the primes 2 and 3. The plan is to rebuild §49 around a smooth cover Σ̃. This is a characteristic-sensitive version of the discrete group-theoretic computations in the Longue Marche, and it seems not to have been developed in the literature.
missed.quote: plus intéressant à prendre comme "primitives" non ξ et η0, mais bien carrément les "primitives" discrètes α0 et β0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral models of the 'lacets' schemes for the modular tower could connect to models of M_{1,1} and the stack issues at 2 and 3. However, the page itself contains only routine linear algebra.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is routine linear algebra: images and determinants of 1−ρ and 1−σ on a rank-2 lattice, plus a change of unknowns. The only mildly interesting feature is the unfinished programme of a smooth integral model Σ̃ (developed on the next page), which is an internal technical step rather than a new result.
transcription_corrections: '{+modulo 2[?]+}' should most likely read '{+de rang 1+}' (inserted above the crossed-out word): id−σ is 'de rang 1 (en toute caractéristique)' for the second endomorphism.
'(— se détruisant[?] en car. 3' plausibly '(se dégénérant en car. 3' or similar; the sense is that id−ρ fails to be invertible in characteristic 3.
In the heading line, the second operator written before τ_M is σ_M (partially overwritten), matching the transcription's ρ_M, σ_M, τ_M.
The first of the earlier 'primitives' (γ2) is overwritten/crossed in the manuscript; the reading 'γ2, γ3 et γ′' is plausible but uncertain.

Phrase '[-On procèdera donc-] {+On arrive+}' is followed by a new sentence, plausibly 'Il paraît plus intéressant de prendre comme "primitives"...'; the '(pour ... [?])' fragment belongs to 'pour le second'.
